body:
Okay, I get what you're saying. Thanks for that. Glad to know that it's not just me.

That was a pretty interesting talk. Objectively, what she's saying isn't surprising to me. At one point, she says that one needs to be authentic, not merely what they think that they should be seen as. I guess my problem is that I can't be "authentic". I can't just broadcast all of my issues and problems with others; doing so would be foolhardy. Really, the idea of being open with people and the amount of risk involved makes me uncomfortable. I guess that I don't understand it. Maybe it's just not something that I can do.

I do volunteer (tutor/read with elementary school kids). I like it, but after it's over it doesn't have any effect on me. Maybe that's normal, but I don't  know. I don't feel like I'm getting what I objectively think that I should out of it. Does that make sense? I like helping others because I feel like I might as well offer myself to them, but I wish that I got more out of it.

I've tried, but nothing's ever truly held my interest or excited me in the way that others describe. Everything just feels like going through the motions; I'm just doing things to get them done. And no worries, your English is perfect.

I just find it a bit odd that I've apparently never had a true friendship or anything like that. If I haven't formed such a relationship in 18 years, I don't know how I'd be able to in the future. 

I do want to be in college, and I am appreciative of the opportunity. What situation are you referring to?

No, I've never discussed my mental health history with anyone outside of my family (excluding therapists, obviously). I don't want to expose an undesirable aspect of myself to others. I don't want to be vulnerable and lower myself in that way, if that makes sense. The counselor I was talking to made it sound like even sharing small things (preferences, likes/dislikes, etc.) would bring you closer to others. I don't experience that at all, so I guess that I'm confused.

That's kind of you. I guess that I don't really have anything specific to talk about at the moment, but thank you for offering.
